entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Brijendra Kumar Raj Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State.

2. By means of this third bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant-Bipin Patel, who is involved in Case Crime No. 91 of 2020, under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)J I.P.C., Section 3/4 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act, Police Station Saini, District Kuashambi, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. First bail application of the applicant was rejected by the coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 13.12.2021 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 1452 of 2021 and second bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 15.03.2023 in Criminal Misc.
Bipin Patel vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69235812/
1 Bail Application No. 19949 of 2022.
4. Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that vide order of this Court dated 15.03.2023 passed in second bail application of the applicant, direction was given to the trial court to make an endeavour to conclude the trial, expeditiously, without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties fixing short dates, but till date, trial of the applicant has not been concluded.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 1452 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text:
Criminal Misc.
Bipin Patel vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. On putting query by the Court with regard to present status of trial of the applicant, learned counsel for the applicant apprised the court that date has been fixed for final argument of the case before the trial court.
6. In view of the above, it is not in dispute that the trial of the applicant is at the verge of completion.
Hence, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail at this stage.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is rejected.
8. It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.
